questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The language was definitely a crucial part of my choice, as well as the fantastic nature and culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, there were many info events.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The University held information events and other exchange students were also of great help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived at Meierwiesenstrasse 62 and even though it seems far away on the map, it was 10 min from the city center by train.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was quite easy since the platform was similar to the one use by KU. It uses the same setup with a checklist of different things you need to do and when you need to do them by.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: UZH was very quick to respond to any questions I had through their contact form.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: This was a very pleasant experience as UZH informed the students about when and how to do what.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Stay informed, especially look out for the registration dates for classes with a maximum number of students. These are often popular.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took master courses as they were in English. This was not a problem as a BA student.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The materials for the courses were different from what I was used to in Copenhagen. At UZH they use many different ways of communication of knowledge such as videos, podcasts, seminars and so on instead of books sometimes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Contract Design I 
- Workshop & Lecture Series on the Law & Economics of Innovation
- German intensive language course certificate (C1)
- European Tax Law 
- International Sales Law (CISG) 
- The Art and Science of Negotiations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
- Contract Design I 
- International Sales Law (CISG) 
- The Art and Science of Negotiations

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Meat is very expensive in Switzerland, we are talking 150 Dkk per kg chicken breast.
You should budget for traveling on the weekends, this is easily between 200-1000 per weekend depending on where you go.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Meat definitely more expensive.
Cell service was not very expensive. Look up Swype, they cost 15-20 chf per month and with the coupon "helloneptun" I got 60 chf for free.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Look up ASVZ. It is also an app with university sports and gyms which are mostly free.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A VERY wide range of sports and activities using the ASVZ app. They were almost all free.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely hiking and skiing. It might be expensive, but since you are already there on an exchange it is the cheapest it will every be in Switzerland.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Matterhorn (Zermatt)
Lausanne
Luzern
Geneva 
Flumserbeg
Arosa
Davos

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Since it is very similar to danish culture I would not worry about it as a problem.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: You have to really be make sure to try and speak to the local students and suggest doing stuff together. Many exchange students will tend to hang around other exchange students as this is very easy.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really, it is quite similar.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The politeness and the importance of being on time.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The written exams are hand written, no computers allowed at all. When that is said it is very different and not something UCPH students are used to, but it is possible and should not discourage anyone from picking UZH.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take the Polybahn sometime, it is an experience in it of itself. Also the "Mensa" cafeterias are very reasonable priced with very nice food.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships I have made along the way as well as the nature I have had the privilege of experiencing.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Definitely the fact that the written exams were hand written, however it is very possible and should not discourage anyone from choosing UZH.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go to Switzerland, you will not regret it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
